quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everyone in the office ___ excited about the new project.
quests.completedSentence: Everyone in the office is excited about the new project.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone' always takes a singular verb, even though it refers to many people at once. The verb here is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Everyone' refers to a whole group, but grammatically it's treated as one unit - singular.
quests.example: Everyone in the office is excited about the new project.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everybody at the reunion ___ ready for the group photo.
quests.completedSentence: Everybody at the reunion seems ready for the group photo.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everybody' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: Don't let the size of the reunion fool you - 'everybody' is still singular.
quests.example: Everybody at the reunion seems ready for the group photo.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everyone on the team ___ a role to play in the presentation.
quests.completedSentence: Everyone on the team has a role to play in the presentation.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: Even though a whole team is involved, 'everyone' is still one grammatical unit.
quests.example: Everyone on the team has a role to play in the presentation.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Someone' / 'somebody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Someone in this building ___ left the lights on again.
quests.completedSentence: Someone in this building has left the lights on again.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Someone' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Someone' points to one unspecified person - always singular.
quests.example: Someone in this building has left the lights on again.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Someone' / 'somebody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Somebody at the front desk ___ always available to help you.
quests.completedSentence: Somebody at the front desk is always available to help you.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Somebody' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Somebody' works exactly like 'someone' for agreement purposes.
quests.example: Somebody at the front desk is always available to help you.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Someone' / 'somebody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Someone from HR ___ these forms every Friday.
quests.completedSentence: Someone from HR reviews these forms every Friday.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Someone' is the singular subject; 'from HR' just describes which person. The verb takes -s: 'reviews'.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on 'someone', not the department name that follows it.
quests.example: Someone from HR reviews these forms every Friday.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Anyone' / 'anybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Anybody who arrives late ___ to wait outside.
quests.completedSentence: Anybody who arrives late has to wait outside.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Anybody' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Anybody' behaves just like 'someone' and 'everyone' - always singular.
quests.example: Anybody who arrives late has to wait outside.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Anyone' / 'anybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Anyone with a valid ticket ___ allowed inside.
quests.completedSentence: Anyone with a valid ticket is allowed inside.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Anyone' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'with a valid ticket' describes 'anyone' - it doesn't change its number.
quests.example: Anyone with a valid ticket is allowed inside.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Anyone' / 'anybody' takes a singular verb, and the base form follows 'does'
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Does anybody here ___ the answer to this question?
quests.completedSentence: Does anybody here know the answer to this question?
quests.grammarRule: 'Anyone' / 'anybody' takes a singular verb, and the base form follows 'does'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Anybody' is singular, which is why the question uses 'does'. Since 'does' already shows the agreement, the main verb stays in its base form: 'know', not 'knows'.
quests.nativeTip: Remember: after 'does', the main verb goes back to its base form.
quests.example: Does anybody here know the answer to this question?

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'No one' / 'nobody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: No one in the meeting ___ the final decision.
quests.completedSentence: No one in the meeting remembers the final decision.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'No one' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'remembers'.
quests.nativeTip: 'No one' means 'not a single person' - that's a singular idea.
quests.example: No one in the meeting remembers the final decision.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'No one' / 'nobody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Nobody on this street ___ what happened last night.
quests.completedSentence: Nobody on this street knows what happened last night.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nobody' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'knows'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Nobody' works the same way as 'no one' for agreement.
quests.example: Nobody on this street knows what happened last night.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'No one' / 'nobody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: No one ___ perfect, but we can still improve.
quests.completedSentence: No one is perfect, but we can still improve.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'No one' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Even standing alone, 'no one' is still grammatically singular.
quests.example: No one is perfect, but we can still improve.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Something' / 'everything' / 'nothing' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Something about this contract ___ suspicious to me.
quests.completedSentence: Something about this contract seems suspicious to me.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Something' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Something' refers to one unspecified thing - always singular.
quests.example: Something about this contract seems suspicious to me.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Something' / 'everything' / 'nothing' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everything in these boxes ___ fragile.
quests.completedSentence: Everything in these boxes is fragile.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everything' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
quests.nativeTip: Even though the boxes contain many items, 'everything' is still one grammatical unit.
quests.example: Everything in these boxes is fragile.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Something' / 'everything' / 'nothing' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Nothing on the menu ___ my dietary restrictions.
quests.completedSentence: Nothing on the menu fits my dietary restrictions.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nothing' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'fits'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Nothing' rules out every option, but it's still a singular subject.
quests.example: Nothing on the menu fits my dietary restrictions.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Much' (uncountable amount) takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Much of the information ___ classified.
quests.completedSentence: Much of the information remains classified.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Much of the information' is singular because 'much' refers to an uncountable amount. The verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Much' describes an uncountable amount, so treat it as singular, just like 'water' or 'information'.
quests.example: Much of the information remains classified.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Much' (uncountable amount) takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Much of the equipment in this lab ___ replacement.
quests.completedSentence: Much of the equipment in this lab needs replacement.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Much of the equipment' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'needs'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Much' pairs with things you can't count individually, like 'equipment' - keep the verb singular.
quests.example: Much of the equipment in this lab needs replacement.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Much' (uncountable amount) takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Much of what she said ___ sense to me.
quests.completedSentence: Much of what she said makes sense to me.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Much of what she said' is treated as singular, so the verb takes -s: 'makes'.
quests.nativeTip: 'What she said' isn't a list of countable items, so 'much' here stays singular.
quests.example: Much of what she said makes sense to me.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Little' (uncountable amount) takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Little of the original building ___ after the fire.
quests.completedSentence: Little of the original building remains after the fire.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Little of the original building' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'remains'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Little' works like 'much' - it's used with uncountable ideas and takes a singular verb.
quests.example: Little of the original building remains after the fire.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Little' (uncountable amount) takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Little of his advice ___ practical in the real world.
quests.completedSentence: Little of his advice seems practical in the real world.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Little of his advice' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'seems'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Advice' can't be counted individually, so 'little' here is singular.
quests.example: Little of his advice seems practical in the real world.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Little' (uncountable amount) takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Little of the data collected so far ___ conclusive.
quests.completedSentence: Little of the data collected so far looks conclusive.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Little of the data' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'looks'.
quests.nativeTip: Even with a long description of the data, 'little' still takes a singular verb.
quests.example: Little of the data collected so far looks conclusive.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Few' (countable amount) takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Few of the applicants ___ the required experience.
quests.completedSentence: Few of the applicants have the required experience.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Few' is used with countable nouns like 'applicants', and it takes a plural verb: 'have'.
quests.nativeTip: Compare 'few' with 'little' from the last level - 'few' is used with countable things and is plural.
quests.example: Few of the applicants have the required experience.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Few' (countable amount) takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Few of his friends ___ where he moved.
quests.completedSentence: Few of his friends know where he moved.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Few of his friends' is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'know'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Friends' can be counted one by one, which is why 'few' here is plural.
quests.example: Few of his friends know where he moved.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Few' (countable amount) takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Few of the tickets ___ still available.
quests.completedSentence: Few of the tickets are still available.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Few of the tickets' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: Tickets are countable items, so 'few' takes the plural verb form here.
quests.example: Few of the tickets are still available.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Several' / 'many' takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Several of the employees ___ requested remote work options.
quests.completedSentence: Several of the employees have requested remote work options.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Several of the employees' is plural, so the verb is 'have'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Several' is always used with countable nouns and takes a plural verb.
quests.example: Several of the employees have requested remote work options.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Several' / 'many' takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Many of the reviews ___ overwhelmingly positive.
quests.completedSentence: Many of the reviews are overwhelmingly positive.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Many of the reviews' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Many' behaves just like 'several' for agreement - both are plural.
quests.example: Many of the reviews are overwhelmingly positive.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Several' / 'many' takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Several of the paintings ___ from the same collection.
quests.completedSentence: Several of the paintings come from the same collection.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Several of the paintings' is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'come'.
quests.nativeTip: Paintings can be counted individually, so 'several' takes the plural verb form.
quests.example: Several of the paintings come from the same collection.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Everyone' / 'everybody' takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Everyone at the conference ___ a badge for security.
quests.completedSentence: Everyone at the conference wears a badge for security.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'wears', even though it refers to a whole conference of people.
quests.nativeTip: Bring back the key trap from this stage: 'everyone' sounds like a crowd, but it's grammatically singular.
quests.example: Everyone at the conference wears a badge for security.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Few' (countable amount) takes a plural verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Few of the guests ___ interested in staying past midnight.
quests.completedSentence: Few of the guests seem interested in staying past midnight.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Few of the guests' is plural, so the verb stays in the base form: 'seem'.
quests.nativeTip: Contrast this with 'everyone' - 'few' is countable and plural.
quests.example: Few of the guests seem interested in staying past midnight.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: 'Much' (uncountable amount) takes a singular verb
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Much of the excitement ___ from the surprise ending.
quests.completedSentence: Much of the excitement comes from the surprise ending.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Much of the excitement' is singular, so the verb takes -s: 'comes'.
quests.nativeTip: As a final check, remember that 'much' pairs with uncountable ideas and stays singular.
quests.example: Much of the excitement comes from the surprise ending.
